transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. 

Um, well, I came in because... I hope this is the right place for this, but I just can't seem to get anything in order anymore. It's a little embarrassing to admit at my age, honestly. My kitchen table right now is just covered with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists. 

I sit there meaning to sort it all out, but I just... I don't know which thing to do first. And then I end up just sitting there until the whole day is gone. I'm so sorry, I don't mean to sound silly or like I'm complaining, but does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you might be able to help me with?
Besides feeling overwhelmed by organizing things, have you noticed any other changes in your memory, like forgetting recent conversations, appointments, or where you put things?

Oh, well... I suppose I do misplace things now and then, but isn't that just a normal part of getting a little older? I really don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill. 

But, um, since you asked... I guess I have been spending quite a bit of time hunting for things I swear I just had in my hand. Like my car keys, or my reading glasses. Oh, and those little appointment cards they give you? They just seem to vanish. Just last week I lost a recipe I was supposed to make for the church supper, and I couldn't find the folder I needed to take to my husband's doctor's office until we were already late. 

I'm sure it's nothing to worry about, though, right? I just need to be a bit more careful, I think. I hope I'm not wasting your time with all this.

Can you tell me when you first started noticing these problems with organizing things and misplacing items—did they begin around the same time as any particular stressful event, like changes in your husband's health, or did they come on gradually over a longer period?

Well, I suppose... I mean, I've always been a little scatterbrained, maybe? Just a little bit. But it really hasn't been this bad... I mean, it hasn't been causing this much trouble for very long. Maybe about a year and three months? Give or take? 

That's right around when my husband started needing a lot more help with his doctor's appointments and just... keeping his daily arrangements straight. It's been a bit of an adjustment, taking all that on. I really should be handling it better, I know. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing a good job for him, you know? It's perfectly normal to feel a little overwhelmed when things change like that, isn't it? I just hope I'm not making too much of a fuss over a normal adjustment period.
Over these past several months, have you been feeling sad, down, or losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, most days?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm sad or... or depressed or anything. I have a wonderful life, really I do. I'm very blessed. 

I still enjoy going to church and seeing my friends at the senior center when I can actually get myself out the door. It's just... well, it's just the organizing and getting things done that's the trouble. I don't sit around crying or feeling sorry for myself, I promise. I try to keep a very positive attitude. I know there are people out there dealing with much worse, so I try not to complain. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to be honest with you that my mood is generally quite fine, really.

Since your husband's health needs increased, have you noticed yourself feeling especially anxious, worried, or on edge—like your heart racing or feeling tense—when you think about all you have to manage?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think so. I mean, I certainly don't get that feeling where my heart is racing out of my chest or anything scary like that. I worry about his health, of course—any wife would, wouldn't they? But I wouldn't say I'm constantly on edge or... or physically tense about it. 

I really try to just take a deep breath and handle what needs handling. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart at the seams or unable to cope! It's really just those silly little mistakes, like losing the paperwork or forgetting what I walked into a room for, that make me feel a bit flustered. But emotionally, I feel quite steady. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions—like thyroid problems, diabetes, vitamin deficiencies, a stroke, or a head injury—that your doctor mentioned could affect your memory or thinking?

Oh, no, I haven't had anything like that. My doctor says I'm actually in very good health for my age, which is such a blessing. 

I mean, I go to all my checkups and they've never mentioned anything about my thyroid, or diabetes, or... or any vitamin issues. And I've certainly never had a stroke or hit my head! I try to take very good care of myself, you know, eating right and taking my daily multivitamin. I wouldn't want to be a burden on anyone. So, physically, I think I'm doing everything exactly the way I'm supposed to. That's a good thing, right? I just wanted to make sure you knew that I'm generally quite healthy otherwise.
Compared to a year and a half ago, would you say these memory and organizing difficulties have been getting steadily worse over time, or have they stayed about the same since they started?

Well, I'd say they've stayed about the same, really. I don't think they're getting worse. I mean, it's just been this sort of constant... well, a constant little struggle since things got busier with my husband. 

I certainly wouldn't say I'm going downhill or anything like that! I'm still managing, you know? It's just the same silly things—the misplaced papers, getting a bit turned around with the schedule. But it hasn't escalated. I'm keeping my head above water, I promise. I try very hard to stay on top of things. I hope that's what you were looking for? I just don't want you to worry that I'm, you know, losing my mind or anything terrible. It's just been a steady sort of... bump in the road.

Do you notice these same kinds of memory slips or trouble organizing things happening in parts of your life that have nothing to do with your husband's care—like your own personal errands, hobbies, or conversations with friends—or does it seem to happen mainly when you're dealing with his appointments and paperwork?

Well, um... I suppose it has bled over a little bit into other things. I mean, I really try to keep it all separate and organized, but... well, I did step down from leading the big spring event at the senior center this year. I just thought, you know, let someone else have a turn! Though, I suppose if I'm being completely honest, I was getting a bit overwhelmed with keeping all those details straight, too. 

And, oh, I feel terrible even saying this, but my daughter... she's such a sweet girl, really... she's started double-checking the bills and my own appointments. I think she just wants to be helpful, of course! But... well, she mentioned she wasn't sure I was keeping it all straight on my own anymore. It's just a little embarrassing, you know? Having your child check up on you like that. But I'm sure it's just a phase while things are so busy, right? I really am trying my best to stay on top of it all. I hope that's the kind of answer you needed?

When you handle tasks like managing your own bills, medications, or finances on your own, do you find you're actually making errors or missing things, or is it more that you feel slower and more flustered but still get them done correctly in the end?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm making real errors, per se. I mean, I'm very careful. I take my time. It just... well, it takes me a bit longer than it used to, that's all. I sit down at the kitchen table with my checkbook and, you know, I just have to look things over an extra time or two to be absolutely sure. 

I do get them done, though! I really do. It just feels a little more... effortful, I guess you could say. A bit more flustered, like you mentioned. But I always make sure the bills are paid and my pills are sorted out eventually. I haven't done anything disastrous, I promise! I just want to make sure I'm doing everything right, you know? Is that... is that normal for someone my age, just slowing down a little bit?
Have you noticed any trouble finding the right words when you're talking, or found yourself repeating the same question to someone because you forgot you'd already asked it?

Oh, goodness, no. I don't think I've had any trouble like that. I mean, everyone forgets a word now and then, don't they? Like... oh, what's the name of that actor, that sort of thing. But no, I haven't been repeating questions or anything silly like that. 

My husband, now, he sometimes asks the same thing twice, but I always just gently remind him. For me, I'm quite sure my conversation is just as it's always been. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my vocabulary! I try very hard to be clear when I speak. I hope I've been making sense today? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me about your sleep lately—are you sleeping well through the night, or do you have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feel very tired and unrefreshed during the day?

Well, um... I think my sleep is mostly fine. I mean, I do toss and turn a little bit sometimes, but that's just because my mind is always going over the things I need to do the next day, you know? Making sure I haven't forgotten anything for my husband. 

But I wouldn't say I have any real trouble. I usually get to sleep eventually, and I'm up and ready to go in the morning. I might feel a tiny bit tired in the afternoon, but I think anyone would with how busy things are! I just push through it and keep going. I really try not to complain about being tired, because I know I have to be strong for him. Does that sound okay? I hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing.
If someone teaches you something new, like how to use a new phone feature or a new recipe, do you find you can remember and use that new information later without much trouble?

Oh, goodness, I think I do just fine with new things! I mean, I might need someone to show me once or twice—especially with those new smart phones, they change everything so fast, don't they? But if my daughter shows me how to send a picture or something, I can usually pick it up. 

I might write it down on a little sticky note just to be safe, so I don't have to bother her again, but I definitely remember how to do it. And recipes, oh, I've been cooking for so long, a new recipe is no trouble at all. I really try my best to keep up with everything. I'm not... I'm not falling behind or anything like that. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job explaining things.

On days or times when you get a break from your husband's care—like when a family member helps out or things are calmer—do you notice your memory and organizing troubles get better, or do they stay just as bad no matter what?

Oh, well... you know, I don't really get very many breaks, if I'm being perfectly honest. My daughter helps when she can, but she's so busy with her own life, I try not to ask too much of her. 

But, um... when things are a little quieter, I suppose I don't really notice a big difference. I mean, I'm always trying my best to keep everything organized, whether it's a busy day or a calm one. I wouldn't say things get... bad, exactly. Just the normal sort of misplacing a paper here or there, which happens to everyone, right? I try so hard to stay on top of it all, I really do. I hope I'm not sounding like I can't handle things... I just want you to know I'm doing my very best. Is that what you meant by your question?

Has your daughter or anyone else actually caught specific mistakes in your bills or medications—like a missed payment or a mixed-up pill—that they had to fix for you, rather than just double-checking your work?

Well, um... I suppose... yes, she has had to step in a little bit. I mean, it's not that I can't do it! It's just that I was so busy, and maybe I missed one or two little things. 

She did find a bill I hadn't paid on time, and... well, she's taken to double-checking my husband's appointments and things like that now. She says it's just to help me out, but I know she's doing it because she doesn't quite trust me to keep it all straight anymore. It's awfully sweet of her, really, but I feel terrible putting that on her. 

And, um, I did have to step down from leading the big spring event at the senior center. I just... I thought it would be best to let someone else handle it this year. I didn't want to let anyone down if I got my papers mixed up. But I'm still helping out! Just not in charge. That's a very sensible thing to do at my age, don't you think? I hope it doesn't make me sound incompetent. I really am trying my hardest to keep everything running smoothly.

Oh, my goodness, I'm so sorry, doctor... did you just ask me another question? I'm afraid I might have missed it just now. I was just sitting here worrying if I'm giving you the right kinds of answers. 

Could you repeat that for me, please? I really do want to make sure I'm being helpful and doing a good job for you. Am I doing all right so far?
Has anyone in your immediate family, like a parent or sibling, ever been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease or another type of dementia?

No, no, thank goodness. Nothing like that in my family. My parents lived to a ripe old age, and they were both sharp as tacks right up until the end. My sister is a few years older than me, and she’s doing just fine, too. 

I mean, we all have those moments where we forget a name or why we walked into a room, right? That’s just part of getting older. But no Alzheimer's or dementia or anything serious like that. I really do think I'm just a little overwhelmed with caring for my husband and trying to keep the house running. That makes sense, doesn't it? I hope that’s a helpful answer for you.

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. 

Um, well, I came in because... I hope this is the right place for this, but I just can't seem to get anything in order anymore. It's a little embarrassing to admit at my age, honestly. My kitchen table right now is just covered with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists. 

I sit there meaning to sort it all out, but I just... I don't know which thing to do first. And then I end up just sitting there until the whole day is gone. I'm so sorry, I don't mean to sound silly or like I'm complaining, but does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you might be able to help me with?

Oh, well... I suppose I do misplace things now and then, but isn't that just a normal part of getting a little older? I really don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill. 

But, um, since you asked... I guess I have been spending quite a bit of time hunting for things I swear I just had in my hand. Like my car keys, or my reading glasses. Oh, and those little appointment cards they give you? They just seem to vanish. Just last week I lost a recipe I was supposed to make for the church supper, and I couldn't find the folder I needed to take to my husband's doctor's office until we were already late. 

I'm sure it's nothing to worry about, though, right? I just need to be a bit more careful, I think. I hope I'm not wasting your time with all this.
